paragraphs.text: DSH plugin: auto-compact long sessions after user idle time, before the KV cache expires.
# dsh-idle-compact [](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that prepares a compaction of a long session while you are away, bef
ore the model provider's KV cache expires, and lets you apply it with one click when you come back.
## Why
Providers cache the prompt prefix of a conversation for a few minutes. While the cache is warm, re-r
eading a long history is cheap. Once it expires, your next message re-bills the whole history at the
full, uncached input price.
If you walk away from a long session, this plugin produces the compaction summary while the cache is
still warm, so that summarization request is cheap. Nothing changes in your session until you decid
o that summarization request is cheap. Nothing changes in your session until you decide to apply it.
## How it works

1. When a session finishes a turn and waits for you, a timer starts.
2. Any new activity in that ses

sion cancels the timer, whether it's you replying or the agent starting work.
3. When the timer fire

s, the plugin prepares a compaction only if all of these hold:
- the agent is still idle and its las

t turn finished normally (not an error or a stop);
- no background job or subagent is running for th
reparing runs exactly the summarization request DSH's `/compact` would make, and keeps the result. Y

our session is not changed.
5. An **Apply compaction** bar appears just above the message input, sho

wing how many history items it covers.
6. Clicking it runs DSH's own `/compact` command, exactly as
if you had typed it, and answers its summarization request with the prepared result, so no new model
call is made. The conversation shows the usual `/compact` card with its "Compacted N history items"
s made. The conversation shows the usual `/compact` card with its "Compacted N history items" reply.
The prepared summary is only valid for the conversation it summarized. If you send another message (
or the history changes in any other way), it is discarded and the button disappears; the next idle p
eriod that qualifies prepares a fresh one. If the conversation somehow differs at the moment you cli
ck, `/compact` makes its own model call instead of using a stale summary.
When the plugin starts or is reloaded (a DSH restart, a plugin update), sessions that are already wa
iting are timed from the end of their last turn. A session idle for less than the idle delay is time
d for only the remaining seconds. A session idle for longer is skipped entirely, because the provide
r's cache has most likely expired and preparing would cost full price. It qualifies again after its
has most likely expired and preparing would cost full price. It qualifies again after its next turn.
Subagent sessions are skipped, because they never wait for a user reply. If the agent is busy when t
he timer fires, nothing is prepared and this is logged.
## Settings
Open **Plugins → Idle Compact** in the DSH Web UI:
| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| Context length threshold (tokens) | `256000` | Prepare a compaction only when the session context

has reached this length. |
| Idle time (seconds) | `300` (5 min) | How long you must go without repl
ying before a compaction is prepared. |
Both fields take whole numbers of at least 1. Changes apply without a restart. A changed idle time t
akes effect the next time a session starts waiting.

## Install
Requires the DSH Web UI. Tested on DSH 0.2.1-alpha.3 and 0.2.1-rc.2; earlier versions are untested.
The plugin uses DSH's authenticated `/api` routes, its settings-form components, and the area above
the message input (`conversation.input.dock`).
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or, in the Web UI, open **Plugins → Add plugin** and enter `github:Arrosam/dsh-idle-compact` or a lo
open **Plugins → Add plugin** and enter `github:Arrosam/dsh-idle-compact` or a local checkout path.
## Token cost
Each prepared compaction makes one summarization call to your model. It's cheap because the cache is
warm, but it is spent even if you never click Apply or never return to that session. If most of you
r idle sessions are ones you abandon, raise the threshold.
Prepared summaries are kept in memory only. Restarting DSH discards them.
## Page endpoints
The browser half talks to the Host over two routes on DSH's own `/api` channel. DSH checks the brows
er's login and origin before either route runs, so other programs and other websites can't use them.
- `GET /api/idle-compact/events?sessionId=<id>`: a server-sent event stream. The first message is th
e session's current state, and another follows each change. Each message is `{ "prepared": false }`,
or `{ "prepared": true, "items": <history items>, "tokens": <approx. tokens>, "applying": <boolean>

}`.
- `POST /api/idle-compact/apply` with JSON `{ "sessionId": "<id>" }` applies the prepared compa
/idle-compact/apply` with JSON `{ "sessionId": "<id>" }` applies the prepared compaction. Responses:
| Status | Body | When |
| 200 | `{ "ok": <boolean>, "result": <command result> }` | `/compact` ran; `ok` is whether it succe

eded. Its outcome also shows in the chat. |
| 200 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "command-unavailable" }`

| The `/compact` command isn't available. |
| 400 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "bad-body" }` | The bod

y isn't a JSON object with a non-empty string `sessionId`. |
| 404 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "no-ses

sion" }` | No live session has that id. |
| 409 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "not-prepared" }` | Nothin

g is prepared, or it went stale. |
| 409 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "applying" }` | An apply is alrea

dy running for that session. |
| 500 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "failed", "message": "…" }` | Applyin
g failed unexpectedly. |

ek-ai` directories) to choose which runtimes to test against.
